passage.title: The Roofs That Cool a City
paragraphs: If you fly over Berlin, Stuttgart or Basel today, you will see something unusual: hundreds of roofs covered with grass, flowers and small plants. Engineers call them green roofs, and cities have been building them for more than forty years.

The idea is simple. When it rains in a normal city, the water runs off the concrete immediately and the drains cannot take it, so the streets flood. A green roof works like a sponge: the plants and the soil hold the water and release it slowly. Studies have shown that a green roof can keep more than half of the rain that falls on it.

Green roofs also cool the air. If a building has a green roof, the temperature inside is two or three degrees lower in summer, so the owners spend less money on air conditioning. Birds and insects come back, and the street is quieter.

They are not perfect. A green roof is heavier than a normal roof, so an old building may need new structural support, and somebody has to look after the plants. But engineers agree on one thing: unless our cities change the way they treat rain, the floods will get worse.

choices: The plants and the soil hold it.
It runs off the concrete and the streets flood.

choices: Because they use less air conditioning.
Because birds and insects come back.

items.stem: What does the text compare a green roof to, and why?

passage.title: A Team Without a Country
paragraphs: At the opening ceremony of the 2016 Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro, one team walked into the stadium without a national flag. The ten athletes of the Refugee Olympic Team came from South Sudan, Syria, Ethiopia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. None of them had a country to represent, because all of them had left their homes because of war.

The most famous member was Yusra Mardini, a swimmer from Damascus. In 2015 she was crossing the Aegean Sea in a small boat with nineteen other people when the engine stopped working. Mardini and her sister, both trained swimmers, got into the water and pushed the boat for more than three hours, until it reached the Greek island of Lesbos.

Nobody from the team has won a medal, and that was never the point. The Olympic Committee has sent a refugee team to every Games since 2016. As the president said in Rio, they have no flag and no anthem, but they have the same right to compete as everybody else.
